qualifier: Yes. Fort Lauderdale requires a permit from its Development Services Department before work on mooring structures, a term its code defines to include seawalls. A substantial repair (more than half the shoreline, or over half the wall's fair market replacement cost) must meet the city's tidal flood barrier height, which is also capped at the FEMA base flood elevation or 6 ft NAVD88. Broward County also requires its own Environmental Resource License, often a general license for a repair in the same place.
detail_rows: City :: A permit from the Development Services Department is required before construction of mooring structures, defined to include a seawall; on navigable waters every regulating authority must also approve, and the applicant certifies ownership of the abutting land or produces the owner's written consent - Code Sec. 8-91(a)(2), (b). The city's Permitting Services FAQ lists seawalls among permits filed with a copy of a current survey and a completed Zoning Affidavit, and a permit renewed before it expires costs 50% of the original fee (100% after expiry). Substantial repair = work along more than 50% of the property's shoreline or over 50% of the wall's fair market replacement cost; docks, finger piers and piles are not counted - ULDR Sec. 47-19.13.C.12. qualifier: Yes. Boca Raton requires a city permit to install or replace a seawall, and no bulkhead or retaining wall may be built in city waters until Development Services approves the plans. qualifier: Yes.
